content.value_statement: React teams need polished motion without rebuilding animation patterns. This skill provides Framer Motion guidance, reusable templates, and examples for Next.js interfaces.
actual_capabilities: Explains Framer Motion setup and basic motion component usage.
Provides examples for variants, gestures, hooks, and reduced motion support.
Covers page transitions for React and Next.js applications.
Includes animated list and reorderable list templates.
Shows scroll-triggered animations and micro-interaction patterns.
limitations: Requires a React project that can install Framer Motion.
Does not benchmark animation performance automatically.
Does not replace accessibility testing for motion-sensitive users.
Examples may need styling adjustments for each design system.

use_cases.title: Add Interface Motion
use_cases.description: Use ready patterns to add entrance, hover, tap, and layout animations to React components.

use_cases.title: Design Page Transitions
use_cases.description: Translate motion ideas into practical Framer Motion patterns for Next.js page flows.

use_cases.title: Standardize Animation Code
use_cases.description: Create consistent animation guidance for teams working across shared React components.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add a simple Framer Motion entrance animation to my React component. Include reduced motion support.

prompt_templates.title: Create List Motion
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design animated add, remove, and reorder behavior for this list. Keep the API reusable.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Page Transitions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to propose page transitions for my Next.js app. Include timing, exit behavior, and accessibility notes.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Motion System
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Framer Motion patterns. Recommend reusable variants, performance improvements, and reduced motion fallbacks.

output_examples.input: A React card needs hover, tap, and entrance motion.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a motion component with spring-based hover and tap states, a short entrance transition, and reduced motion handling.

output_examples.input: A Next.js product page needs transitions between route views.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines a transition wrapper, exit timing, shared layout IDs, and mobile performance checks.

output_examples.input: A task list needs animated insert, remove, and reorder behavior.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests AnimatePresence for entry and exit, Reorder for dragging, and stable item keys for smooth updates.

best_practices: Respect reduced motion preferences before adding movement-heavy effects.
Use variants to keep shared animation states consistent across components.
Prefer transform and opacity animations for smoother rendering.
anti_patterns: Do not animate layout properties when transforms can create the same result.
Do not add long transitions that slow navigation or repeated workflows.
Do not rely on animation to communicate critical information alone.

faq.question: Does this skill install Framer Motion?
faq.answer: It provides installation guidance, but installation still requires user approval in the project environment.

faq.question: Can it work with Next.js App Router?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples include page transition patterns for Next.js App Router projects.

faq.question: Does it cover accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It repeatedly recommends reduced motion support and simpler motion for sensitive users.

faq.question: Can it build reusable animation components?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes templates for page transitions, animated lists, reorderable lists, and drag handles.

faq.question: Does it include design system styling?
faq.answer: It includes Tailwind-style examples, but teams should adapt styles to their own design system.

faq.question: Is it limited to simple animations?
faq.answer: No. It also covers variants, gestures, hooks, shared layouts, scroll animations, and micro-interactions.
